citations.quote: ECOG 2 (ambulatory, capable of self‑care but unable to carry out work activities)

candidates.description: A scale used to assess the functional status of cancer patients.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify the numerical value following 'ECOG' in the general findings or assessment sections.
candidates.measurement_definition: The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale, where 0 represents fully active, 1 represents restricted in physically strenuous activity, and 2 represents ambulatory and capable of self-care but unable to carry out work activities.
candidates.name: ECOG Performance Status
candidates.uncertainty: The exact mapping of patients to the full 0-5 scale is limited by the provided excerpts, which primarily show scores 1 and 2.

candidates.description: A ratio calculated from the absolute counts of neutrophils and lymphocytes, often used as a systemic inflammatory marker.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Locate 'NLR' within the CBC or laboratory data sections and extract the associated numeric value.
candidates.measurement_definition: The absolute neutrophil count divided by the absolute lymphocyte count, typically reported as a decimal value.
candidates.name: Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR)
candidates.uncertainty: It is uncertain whether NLR was calculated consistently across all patients or only recorded when identified as elevated.

limitations: The dataset consists of a small number of patients, limiting the ability to identify rare baseline variables.
NLR is not recorded for all patients, which may introduce selection bias in its availability.
summary: The evidence supports the identification of ECOG performance status and the Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR) as measurable baseline clinical variables in patients with metastatic KRAS-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
